findings.title: S3 bucket exposes or allows public access configuration
findings.description: Public ACLs and/or S3 Block Public Access not fully enabled increases risk of data exposure.
findings.remediation_hint: Enable all four Block Public Access settings; remove public ACLs; use CloudFront OAC for public content.

findings.title: Default encryption not configured for bucket
findings.description: Objects may be stored without default SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS at rest.
findings.remediation_hint: Enable default bucket encryption; prefer KMS CMK for sensitive data with key policies.

findings.title: S3 versioning not enabled
findings.description: Without versioning, accidental deletes and ransomware-style overwrites are harder to recover from.
findings.remediation_hint: Enable versioning on critical buckets; pair with lifecycle rules and MFA delete for sensitive buckets.

findings.title: Server access logging not enabled
findings.description: Bucket-level access logging to a dedicated log bucket aids detection and forensics.
findings.remediation_hint: Enable server access logging to a centralized logging bucket with tight bucket policy.

findings.title: Bucket policy allows anonymous or public object access
findings.description: A bucket policy statement grants GetObject (or s3:*) to a public principal.
findings.remediation_hint: Remove Principal *; use OAI/OAC, signed URLs, or authenticated viewers only.

findings.title: Overly broad bucket policy (account root with s3:*)
findings.description: Granting s3:* to account root bypasses normal IAM boundary discipline and is hard to audit.
findings.remediation_hint: Replace with roles, explicit ARNs, and condition keys (aws:PrincipalArn, vpc SourceIp).
